The problem with the Hubble mirror was the Reflective Null Corrector (RNC) which was used to measure the shape of the Hubble main mirror during construction was positioned incorrectly. The RNC has to be exactly the right distance from the main mirror in order to produce the right result. To achieve this they used a rod of known length (and thermally corrected) then an optical interferometer to measure the final offset. The interferometer bounced light off the polished end of the rod. To ensure the light bounced off the correct spot on the rod a cap was produced which centered the rod and had a hole for the light to pass through. The instructions said to paint the cap black (so it would not reflect any light itself). Apparently the technician didn't have paint and in a rush just used black tape and cut a hole in it. Unfortunately in cutting the hole he produced a burr which reflected the light and caused the interferometer to measure the wrong spot. This resulted in the distance being off a mm or so and a mirror perfectly ground to the wrong spec.

The sad part is after the mirror was finished it was transferred to the final 3 point mounting system used by the telescope itself and remeasured with a different null corrector. This measurement consistently showed the half wavelength spherical aberration. Unfortunately since the aberration was so consistent people blamed the error either on the 3 point mount not being able to support the mirror properly on the ground or the different null corrector.
